clues: This place hugs the sea at the foot of steep mountains in the far northwest. A huge ice field caps the peaks, and ice rivers flow down from it.
Warm ocean water flows past this place, and coast mountains block the sea air. The trapped air turns mild and wet, so rain forests grow here.
In 1906, this place took over as the seat of government from the old port of Sitka. Lawmakers had ordered the move six years before, in 1900.
No road links this place to the rest of its state or the rest of the land. Boats and planes are the only ways to get here.
The governor of Alaska has an office in this place. The state lawmakers of Alaska meet here too.
